last_material_result: One bounded three-wedge distribution check was completed. (1) Route-specific party-size queries such as Seoul-Busan/Seoul-Gangneung with 3 people surfaced mostly timetable, fare and static travel articles rather than an interactive party-size crossover calculator, so this wedge survives. (2) Holiday/family variants are more content-saturated and vulnerable to constantly changing congestion/discount conditions; keep only as a secondary seasonal landing-page angle, not the core product. (3) Destination-day-trip/local-mobility variants showed the strongest differentiation: current travel pages often explain that rail arrival still leaves local taxi/transit/rental needs, while car-friendly destinations introduce parking and congestion tradeoffs. This creates a calculable missing layer: include destination-side mobility cost/time and show when bringing a car changes the total trip economics. A sponsored 부산 transport comparison and current 강릉/부산 travel guides confirm the decision is already framed around whole-trip convenience, not just intercity fare. No evidence yet requires paid routing APIs; preset routes plus editable assumptions remain sufficient for a smoke-test MVP.
economics: KRW0 validation spend. Monetization thesis remains ads plus parking/rental-car/travel affiliate and portfolio cross-promotion. Best acquisition model is a long-tail matrix of route x party size x trip type pages feeding one reusable calculator. Expected micro-asset contribution remains KRW10k-50k/month if organic traffic is obtained cheaply; no subscription thesis and no paid API dependency assumed.
next_checkpoint: Next run: validate data-maintenance feasibility and construct a minimal preset schema for 3 archetypes only (Seoul-Busan city trip, Seoul-Gangneung local-mobility trip, Seoul-Jeonju day trip): rail/bus fare, road distance, toll, representative parking, station first/last-mile and destination local-mobility assumptions with user override. recommendation: KEEP and narrow toward party-size crossover plus destination-side mobility cost. Treat route-specific SEO as primary distribution, holiday content as secondary. Do not BUILD yet; complete one data-maintenance feasibility round first.
